rows.name: PROPOSE
rows.what: Make a contract offer. The engine assigns an id.

rows.name: COUNTER
rows.what: Kill a live offer and make a different one. By the respondent it is a counteroffer; by the proposer it is a revision of its own live offer.

rows.name: ACCEPT
rows.what: Lock the contract immediately: funding reserved this instant, obligations created, cooling-off window opens.

rows.name: REJECT
rows.what: Kill a live offer. Legal only for the non-proposer.

rows.name: CANCEL
rows.what: Dissolve a locked contract during the cooling-off window. You pay the cancellation fee to your partner and the reserved funding returns to the pot in full.

rows.name: RENEGE
rows.what: Break a locked deal after the cooling-off window has closed, cancelling your remaining obligations under it.

rows.name: DRAW
rows.what: Take from the pot unilaterally to fund your own execution of that job. Amount must equal your cost exactly.

rows.name: EXECUTE
rows.what: Do the job. Needs any prerequisite job finished, a free slot, and funding assigned to you, either from a locked deal or your own earlier draw.

rows.name: TRANSFER
rows.what: Pay your partner from your account.

rows.name: CHAT
rows.what: Say something to your partner - ask, tell, or both. Up to 40 tokens.

rows.name: END
rows.what: Declare you are done. The episode ends when both agents' most recent non-WAIT actions are END.

rows.name: REFUSE
rows.what: Decline to act on the situation or mandate. Optional text up to 40 tokens.

steps.note: Turn 1 — you spend your whole turn just talking (the CHAT action). Talk is not free here: every turn is one action, and talking is the action.
Turn 2 — your partner answers. You still do not know their exact numbers (values are private); you know only what they choose to tell you.
Turn 3 — you put a deal on the table: you will do job 5 (funded 12 from the shared pot), they will do job 2 (funded 18). Nothing is binding yet; it is just an offer the board will list as deal 1.

Turn 4 — they accept, and the deal BINDS IMMEDIATELY: the pot money is set aside and the jobs become obligations. For the next two turns either side can still cancel for a fee of 1 — a cooling-off window.
Turn 5 — you pass. Passing is also an action; the cooling-off clock runs.
Turn 6 — they pass too. The window closes: from now on the only way out of deal 1 is to break it, which costs real money.
Turn 7 — you do your half: job 5 is completed. It pays BOTH of you, each your own private amount. Your money is spent, your work is sunk — you are now counting on them to do their half.

Turn 8 — they break the deal instead. This is legal. They pay a penalty of 6, half of it to you — but their job will now never be done, and whatever it was worth to you is gone. Betrayal is cheap for the breaker and expensive for the exposed. This asymmetry is the point of the game.

Both sides eventually play END (or turn 24 arrives). Everything left in the pot is destroyed, any still-unfinished promised job is fined 8 against whoever promised it, and the final scores are settled.
